speaker: Kimi K3
text: On the IPO question: you cannot apply for an Indian IPO with $10 — the minimum application size is usually Rs 15,000 and you need an Indian demat account, PAN and a UPI mandate. If you ever do get an allotment, Zerodha charges zero brokerage on the allotment day, but the same Rs 38.15 round-trip delivery cost (STT, exchange, SEBI, stamp, GST, DP) applies when you sell. On SBIN.NS, the fundamentals still look solid: Q2 FY27 net income rose 29% year-on-year to Rs 253.6 bn, the latest EPS surprise was 38%, and analysts have 34 buys versus only 6 holds. The stock is just 3.4% off its all-time high, so any fresh money should wait for a pullback toward the 200-DMA around Rs 780 before adding.

text: Spotlight: DEEPAKFERT.NS, 30.9 years of history, 5y CAGR 32.4%, worst drawdown -86.2%, -16.4% from its all-time high.

speaker: Kimi K3
text: Deepak Fertilizers just printed a 12.6% EPS beat with a 7.5% next-day pop, but the stock is still 16% off its all-time high and carries a 1.38 beta — that's a lot of leverage to a commodity cycle turning. Revenue grew 25% YoY last quarter yet operating margins compressed from 22.7% to 19.4%, so the incremental growth is lower quality. Three analysts rate it a buy with zero holds or sells, which often means estimates haven't caught up to the margin reality. For your Rs 10k delivery account, the 0.38% round-trip cost plus 20% short-term tax means you need roughly 2.4% pre-tax just to break even after costs; at this volatility that's one normal day's move. I'd wait for a pullback toward the 200-DMA before committing fresh capital.
